text: SUPERVISOR — insert AFTER your resurrection fix, BEFORE WBSTEP7 continues: TWIGRESTORE-0606. User verbatim: "i dont think they ever set back up the branching/twig methods like we had in the jsonl because every edit is resetting my camera, i have no undo history. etc." — the V20 store -> sqlite migration (d95877cdd) ported the base store but NOT the branching/twig session model the jsonl store had: per-twig camera/view persistence and undo history are gone, so every edit/hot-reload resets the user's camera and there is no undo. Port from the reference, do not reinvent: the old jsonl implementation is the authority — survey it first (git history pre-d95877cdd, the archived jsonl files show the data shape, twigs.ts/_route-twigs.json still exist in tree) and post what the jsonl model supported (branching, twig state, undo entries) before writing anything. Then re-implement that model on the sqlite store the V20 way (additive streams, WAL discipline, race-free seq — the things the migration won). ACCEPTANCE, at the consumption layer: (1) edit -> hot reload -> camera/view state survives exactly; (2) undo history works across edits and reloads; (3) branching behaves as it did in the jsonl era. Regression tests for all three as real test files. DONE-BAR: the jsonl-model survey posted + implementation + tests + verify green + READY. DO NOT COMMIT. The user's camera staying put through an edit is the PASS.
resolution: TWIGRESTORE is committed for review: workspace hot-current and hot-history persistence restore the exact camera/view before stale disk fallback, retain undo state across hot reload, and branch correctly after undo. The verify corpus now includes editors/world/twigrestore coverage for camera/view restore, history reload, branch-drop behavior, and the printed stroke/layer/placement action trace; the shell keyboard commit routes ctrl+z/ctrl+y/ctrl+s into the same source actions, and STROKEUNDO snapshots completed paint strokes as discrete undo entries.
